newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FOREX MARKET MIXED, WARY OF NEXT CBANK MOVE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FOREX MARKET MIXED, WARY OF NEXT CBANK MOVE.

text.p: Slovak forex traders said they remain wary of what appears to be the central bank's intention to keep the market guessing, as the crown stays close to parity with its mark/dollar basket after a mixed month.

"I see no clear trend of the crown now, but there will never be one, because as soon as one is shaping it triggers a speculative follow up, which the central bank does not favour," Martin Macko, a chief dealer at Istrobanka, said.

The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) ended drawing more or less a sine curve after a month on Thursday, fixing the crown at its parity, then hitting a maximum 0.6 percent depreciation against the basket and then a 0.26 percent appreciation.

"Such a curve on such a relatively normal market characterises a balanced market, but whether the midpoint is its peak is not clear yet, though some appear to rely on it," said Robert Hakszer, a chief dealer at Slovenska Sporitelna.

Slovak forex dealers said they estimated some $50-100 million flowed in from abroad after a break on Wedensday, and foreign currency selling continued on Thursday though at a "bit" moderate pace, leaving the market mixed.
The NBS fixed the crown at 30.908 to the dollar and at 20.357 to the mark, implying virtual parity with the mark/dollar basket, after an appreciation of 0.24 percent on Wednesday.
"We expected the (fix) move already yesterday, but it seems good (to NBS) when foreign speculators do not know where North is," Hakszer added.
"I think the crown could strengthen slightly, but I do not expect anything special," said Vladimir Akubzanov, a dealer with VUB Bank.
The NBS fixes the crown daily against a 60/40 percent mark/dollar basket within plus/minus five percent of the basket's midpoint.
Market talk about a possible crown devaluation have not receded, despite Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar rejecting any intention to weaken the crown to boost exports last month.

The Slovak trade deficit for the first seven months of the yea widened to 31.895 billion crowns, from 26.97 billion for the January-June period, boosted by growing imports, especially in consumer items.
